data.name: Galal
data.gender_notes: Galal is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: This name is derived from the Arabic root 'G-L-L', meaning 'to continue, to persist'. In the Quran, Allah (swt) uses this name to refer to His promise and commitment to His creation. The name Galal carries the meaning “Continuity, Perpetuity” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Galal usually hope their child will grow to embody continuity, perpetuity and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that signifies the promise and commitment of Allah (swt) to His creation.
data.etymology: Galal belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Continuity, Perpetuity.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Galal total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Abi Dhi'ab al-Khawlani, a prominent early Islamic scholar and narrator of Hadith, was given the name Galal ibn Abdullah al-Khawlani during his lifetime. He was born in Khawlan, a region in modern-day Yemen, around 703 AD. Galal is known for his extensive knowledge in various branches of Hadith and is considered a reliable transmitter.

Galal ibn Ibrahim al-Farghani, an astronomer and mathematician during the Abbasid Caliphate, is also known by this name. He lived during the late 8th and early 9th centuries AD and is recognized for his significant contributions to mathematics and astronomy, particularly his work on trigonometry and the calculation of lunar conjunctions.
